solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Generous daughter giving backing to family

indicators.note: to back something is to stand behind it, so this piece is placed after the other

blocks.note: your kin are your family
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter generously supports her family financially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' suggests reversal, but nothing is turned round: the daughter simply stands behind the family, so D goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A generous person and a kind person are both warm-hearted and giving; the words are close synonyms.

clue.text: A region developed [in] time gone by

indicators.note: something developed has been changed and reworked from its original state, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An area that grew and prospered in some earlier era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Developed' reads as describing the region's growth, but it is the signal to rearrange 'A region'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Age is a prehistoric period, a stretch of history long past, when iron tools came into use.

clue.text: Composer unhappy about touring UK

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so these letters are read in the opposite direction
a tour goes all the way round a place, so one piece travels around the other

blocks.note: unhappy means sad
taken as written

explanation.surface: A miserable composer goes on a concert tour of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: The two indicators work in turn: first flip the mood word, then wrap it round the country. Dukas is a French composer less familiar than most crossword regulars.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Dukas was a French composer, best known for The Sorcerer's Apprentice; the definition names his profession.

clue.text: One appeals to the people, and to pupils? Wrong

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order or incorrect, so these letters need rearranging to be right

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher's appeal to parents and pupils is judged to be a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'to' makes the definition and the fodder look like one parallel phrase; the break comes after 'people'.
explanation.definitionFit: A populist is a politician who claims to represent ordinary citizens and courts popular support against elites.

clue.text: Favourite school subject, first on timetable

indicators.note: the first thing on a list is at its head, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: PE is physical education, a school subject
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A pupil's favourite lesson comes first thing on the timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as one school scene, but 'Favourite' alone is the definition, used as an adjective or noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet project or pet subject is one especially loved, so pet serves as an informal synonym for preferred.

clue.text: French friend about to go wandering near Nice, oddly

indicators.note: about here means around, so one piece wraps round the rest
near means next to, so these two pieces sit side by side
oddly picks out the odd-numbered positions, so only letters one, three and so on are kept

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
to rove is to wander about
first and third letters of the French city

explanation.surface: A French friend goes rambling around the Riviera close to Nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French friend' tempts AMI, but 'French' is the definition; 'wandering' and 'oddly' look like anagram signals but are not. The friend is split open to hold the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Provencal describes something from Provence, a region in the south of France, so it is a more specific word for French.

clue.text: Devilish sort, cruel if aroused

indicators.note: to be aroused is to be stirred up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A nasty character who turns vicious when provoked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aroused' reads as provoked to anger, but it signals the rearrangement of 'cruel if'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucifer is a name for Satan, the Devil himself, so he is the very embodiment of a devilish type.

clue.text: Small implement [to make] a low seat

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a tool is an implement

explanation.surface: A little tool used for building a low chair.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests carpentry, but the pieces simply join: S then TOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A stool is a simple backless seat, often short, with legs and no arms.

clue.text: We hear spaniel, also bird

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so the letters come from pronunciation rather than spelling

blocks.note: a cocker is a breed of spaniel, and too means also

explanation.surface: Someone reports a dog and a bird together.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in a non-rhotic British accent, 'cocker too' sounds just like the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockatoo is a crested parrot from Australasia, so it is a particular kind of bird.

clue.text: Chef[‘s] business satisfactory

blocks.note: CO is short for company
OK means acceptable

explanation.surface: A restaurant chef's trade is doing adequately.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is a professional who prepares food, which is exactly what a cook does in a kitchen.

clue.text: Spoils one section of The Planets suite

definitions.text: one section of The Planets suite

blocks.note: first meaning: damages or ruins, a verb

blocks.clueFragment: one section of The Planets suite
blocks.note: second meaning: the opening movement of Holst's orchestral work

explanation.surface: A performance of Holst's Planets is ruined in one movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoils' could be a noun, the loot of war, which fits the Bringer of War; here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar is to blemish or damage, and Mars, the Bringer of War, is the first movement of Holst's The Planets.

clue.text: Decline a season with no commitments?

blocks.note: first meaning: a rapid, uncontrolled drop, as of prices
second meaning, humorous: an autumn when you are not busy

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a stretch of time free of obligations.
explanation.walkthrough: Fall is the American word for autumn, and free means unoccupied; the question mark flags the playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A free fall is a sudden steep slump, as in shares or popularity, so it matches a sharp decline.

clue.text: Predicts pro will join English acting groups

blocks.note: to be pro something is to be for it
E is the abbreviation for English
a cast is the group of actors in a production

explanation.surface: A soothsayer foresees a professional joining English theatre companies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pro' looks like a professional, but it is the preposition meaning in favour of.
explanation.definitionFit: To forecast is to say in advance what will happen, as with the weather; it is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Guide soldiers approaching hill

blocks.note: soldiers are the men of an army
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A guide leads troops towards a hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guide' could be a verb in the surface, but the answer is the noun for an adviser.
explanation.definitionFit: A mentor is an experienced adviser who counsels and trains someone less experienced.

clue.text: High-ranking pilot lost over north east

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray and out of place, so these letters must be put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
NE is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A senior pilot has got lost flying above north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, so the rearranged pilot sits on top of NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-line means leading or of the highest quality, as a top-line performer is among the most senior and important.

clue.text: Water bottle a waiter ultimately carried into bistro

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept
to be carried into a place is to be brought inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: taken as written
the closing letter of the word
a bistro is a small restaurant, like a cafe

explanation.surface: A waiter brings a jug of water to the table in a bistro.
explanation.walkthrough: A plus R goes inside CAFE, between its C and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is an open-topped glass jug for serving water or wine at table.

clue.text: Face cloth [and] soft soap

blocks.note: first meaning: a small towel for washing, British usage
second meaning: flattery or evasive talk

explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft soap' looks like something to use with a face cloth in the bathroom, but it means smooth persuasive talk. In Britain a flannel is a washcloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A flannel is a washcloth, and flannel is also British slang for flattering or evasive waffle.

clue.text: Hot town with harbour, west-facing, one near California

indicators.note: in an across entry west is leftward, so facing west means reading right to left
near means beside, so the pieces are set next to each other

blocks.note: a port is a harbour town
I is the Roman numeral for one
Cal is an abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: A sweltering harbour town on the west coast close to California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' tempts H, but it is the definition. In an across answer, facing west means reading from right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropical describes the steamy heat of the regions near the equator, so it is a stronger word for sweltering weather.

clue.text: Greek character holds in a wild animal

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: rho is the Greek letter R
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Greek person keeps a savage beast indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person from Greece, but it is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhino is a large horned mammal of Africa and Asia that lives in the wild.

clue.text: Some cheating [in] early part of competition

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the letters are a portion of the following word

blocks.note: letters two to five of the word

explanation.surface: A bit of foul play happens in the early rounds of a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'cheating'.
explanation.definitionFit: A heat is a preliminary round, as in athletics, whose winners go through to later rounds.

clue.text: To seek a free ride [is] a problem

blocks.note: first meaning: to thumb a lift from passing drivers
second meaning: a snag or difficulty

explanation.surface: Getting something for nothing causes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a moral about freeloading; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To hitch is short for hitchhike, travelling by begging lifts, and a hitch is a snag that holds things up.

clue.text: Small car heads for Milan in northern Italy

indicators.note: the head of a word is its start, so only the opening letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A little car drives towards Milan in the north of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mini is a small British car first built in 1959.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mini is a famous compact British car model, so the answer names a specific small car.

clue.text: Yelling “Be quiet” before trip

blocks.note: sh is what you say to demand silence
an outing is a short trip

explanation.surface: A teacher yells for quiet before a school trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted words are what a teacher might yell; the quotation marks signal that they are the thing actually said.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouting and yelling both mean crying out loudly; the words are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Love taking business newspaper regularly

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
the FT is the Financial Times, a British business daily

explanation.surface: Someone loves getting the financial paper delivered every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks like an instruction to take alternate letters, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Oft is a poetic or old-fashioned form of often, meaning frequently or many times.

clue.text: Several having rest disturbed [in] English county

indicators.note: things disturbed are moved from their places, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: some means several
taken as written

explanation.surface: Several people have their sleep broken while staying in the English countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset is a rural county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is one of the counties of England, lying in the south-west between Devon and Bristol.

clue.text: Manchester-based orchestra slightly too big for this concert venue

indicators.note: being slightly too big means one small bit too many, so a letter must be dropped to fit

blocks.note: the Halle, with an accent on its E, is a symphony orchestra from Manchester

explanation.surface: A Manchester orchestra finds a concert venue a bit too small for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' points to the answer itself: the orchestra's name is one letter longer than the venue word, so its final E goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall is a large room or building for concerts and public events, such as a concert hall.
